---
title: "Teaching"
---

Currently I teach in three courses at Eindhoven University of Technology: Behavioural Research Methods 2 (BRM2), Behavioural Research Methods 3 (BRM3) and Metascience.

### Behavioural Research Methods 2 (BRM2):

- Covariate Selection in Multiple Regression: Exploratory vs. Confirmatory Approaches (Coming soon)

- [Introduction to multiple regression](https://cristianmesquida.github.io/multiple_regression/). This lecture
introduces multiple regression analysis, including model specification, interpretation of regression coefficients,
model assumptions, and practical applications in R.


- [Introduction to power analysis](https://cristianmesquida.github.io/doing_power_analysis/) (Chapters 1-5). This
lecture covers the principles of statistical power analysis, its role in study design, and how to perform power
analyses for common statistical tests using R. The slides are available [here](https://github.com/cristianmesquida/power_analysis_brm2-3).

### Behavioural Research Methods 3 (BRM3):
[P-values and Bayes Fctors](https://cristianmesquida.github.io/pvalues_and_bayes/slides.pdf). This lecture compares
Frequentist and Bayesian approaches to statistical inference. Students learn how to interpret *p*-values and Bayes
factors and perform Bayesian analyses for paired and independent-samples *t*-tests.


[Advanced power analysis](https://cristianmesquida.github.io/doing_power_analysis/) (Chapters 6-8). This lecture focuses on power analysis for more advanced study designs,
including equivalence tests using the `TOSTER` package, factorial designs using the `Superpower` package, and
simulation-based approaches in R. The slides are available [here](https://github.com/cristianmesquida/power_analysis_brm2-3).


### Metascience

[Introduction to meta-analysis](https://github.com/cristianmesquida/introduction_to_meta-analysis). This lecture introduces the principles of meta-analysis, including effect size estimation, model fitting in R, interpretation of results, and key methodological considerations such as heterogeneity and publication bias.

Bias detection in meta-analysis. This lecture will cover methods for detecting and assessing bias in meta-analyses, including publication bias, selective reporting, and risk of bias, using R. (Coming soon)
